resources.string: Allow access to all files so APK Toolbox can work with APKs in shared storage.
Allow APK Toolbox to install apps so clones can be installed and updated right from here.
No clones yet. Installed clones will show up here.
This file is not a valid APK
An app with this package name is already installed and is signed with another key: the clone cannot be installed over it. Give the clone another package name or remove the installed app.
Use at least two dot-separated parts made of letters, digits and underscores
The clone is signed with APK Toolbox\'s key, not the original one: a signature stops matching once the app is modified.
Nothing: the original is not installed

A clone is rebuilt from the installed original, so it stops being updated when the original is removed - and Google Play hands its files to nobody else. APK Toolbox can look the app up by its package in stores that carry the same builds (APKPure, RuStore, Galaxy Store and others, one after another) and keep the clone up to date from there, in the Sources tab. The original can then be removed. An update signed by someone else than the original is refused.
Background checks are inexact. Doze, battery/network constraints, and device restrictions may delay them.
Updates available: %1$s. Tap to open the clones list.
Start Shizuku and come back. Until then the standard method is used.
APK Toolbox uses Shizuku to install and update clones without prompts. Grant access to enable it; until then the standard method is used.
Play Protect may get in the way

While it is on, clones are not updated in the background by this method: you get a notification and update by hand. Apps from sources are not affected. Turning app scanning off lifts the limit but lowers the protection of the device.
Apps installed through APK Toolbox, clones included, are updated without confirmation.
In the background, on schedule. You get a notification about what was found.
Could not update: %1$s (%2$s). Tap to open the clones list.
No split apps found. Pick a bundle (APKS, XAPK, APKM) or several split APKs below.
Merged, not signed. An unsigned APK cannot be installed until it is signed.
Merged, left unsigned: this app is protected by PairIP and checks its own integrity, so a re-signed build will crash on start.
These splits have a different version or package than the base: %1$s. Deselect them, or turn on merging mismatched splits.
This does not look like a split APK. Pick a bundle (APKS, XAPK, APKM, ZIP) or at least two APKs.
What to do with these files?
A check is running; the result will come as a notification
Legacy key retained only to update clones from older APK-Toolbox versions. New builds use this installation\'s private key.
The saved key could not be decrypted. Import its backup to keep updating clones signed with it, or explicitly reset the key; resetting may break clones and lose their data.
%1$s\nSHA-256 %2$s…\nExport it and keep the file: without it, clones signed with this key cannot be updated after the app is reinstalled.
A new private key was created
Changing or losing this key prevents in-place updates of clones signed with it and may require reinstalling them, which can lose clone data. Export a backup first. APK Toolbox provides no warranty.
Mark the icon with a dot
This app cannot be merged on the device: its resource tables (%1$d MB) need more memory than Android gives an app. Deselecting splits you do not need may help; otherwise merge it on a computer.
New versions of apps from the Sources tab.
No tracked apps yet.\nAdd one by its link or find it through search.
A clone is outdated when its original was updated or its source has a newer version.
Updates of apps from sources and of clones are looked for every time APK Toolbox is opened.
Updates found on mobile data are installed once Wi-Fi is connected.
Updates found on battery are installed once the charger is connected.
Tokens, counted releases, import and export.
When on, takes priority over the other installation methods. Installs from the background may have to ask the root manager for access each time. Not tested.
How updates are installed in the background.
Installs APKS, XAPK and APKM bundles and sets of split APKs. An installed app from the list can be exported as an APKS file.
Merges an app made of several split APKs into one ordinary APK. Only apps installed as splits are listed; a bundle file can be picked as well.
Re-signs the files with the key from the settings. Needed when they were modified or their signature is broken; the app then cannot update over the original.
Signs the merged APK with the key from the settings so it can be installed. Without it the file is left unsigned.
Merges splits even when their versions or packages differ. Use only if the normal merge refuses; the result may not work.
Tracks apps from GitHub, F-Droid, stores and other sites: add an app by link or by name, and new versions are found, downloaded and installed from here.
Makes a copy of an installed app under another package name: every copy has its own data. Pick an app from the list or an APK file.
The clones you have made are here. A clone becomes outdated when its original is updated or a new version appears in its source.
The app speaks the language of the system unless told another.
What was checked, downloaded, cloned, merged and installed, and what failed. Kept for 30 days.
All clones are up to date
Everything the original asks for. Switch off what the clone should not have; the app may stop working without a permission it relies on.
The app asks for no permissions.
The last build could not apply %1$s: the original\'s signing certificate could not be read, so the patch is not in the clone.
Patches to the clone\'s code. Every patch is applied only to this clone and can make the app crash.
Rewrites the package name in the clone code so it finds its own files and components. Mimicry, the other way round, presents the clone as the original to checks.
The clone presents itself as the ORIGINAL entirely - package name and signature: to its own checks, servers and analytics. Lookups of the clone\'s own components keep working through a fallback.

Every call that would end the app - System.exit, Runtime.exit, Process.killProcess, finish, finishAffinity, finishAndRemoveTask - becomes a no-op, so the app cannot kill itself or throw the user out, whatever the reason: a signature check, no account signed in, a failed startup check. After logout the app may stay in the background instead of closing.
Checks inside the clone see the original\'s signature, while it keeps its own name. The patch is part of mimicry, but sometimes it is needed on its own.
Not asked for by this version. Stays off if it comes back.
